Title: pgAdmin prompts for DB password when pgpass file is configured.
URL: https://github.com/pgadmin-org/pgadmin4/issues/9969
Published: N/A
Author: N/A
Highlights:
> Hi @krekel (and @felixtoe) — thanks for the report. This is intended behavior in some configurations and a UX gap in others, and the difference is exactly where the security boundary sits. Quick question first, then explanation:
> 
> **Could you confirm: are you running pgAdmin in Desktop mode (the standalone app on your own machine) or Server mode (the web app on a server that multiple users log into)?** The answer changes whether this is a bug or a deliberate safety choice.
> 
> ## What's actually happening
> 
> pgAdmin currently shows the password prompt unless it knows about credentials through one of these explicit channels: a saved password (`save_password`), a per-server `passfile` parameter set in the server registration, a `passexec_cmd`, or a `service` name. **It does NOT check the default `~/.pgpass` (POSIX) / `%APPDATA%\postgresql\pgpass.conf` (Windows) location.**
> 
> When you press OK with an empty password, pgAdmin connects with `password=''`. **libpq itself** (the underlying PostgreSQL client library, completely separate from pgAdmin) then sees an empty password and does its own pgpass lookup at its built-in default location. That's the layer where your credentials are found. That's why the connection succeeds despite the prompt — the prompt and the actual authentication path are in two different layers.
> 
> ## Why pgAdmin doesn't auto-check `~/.pgpass`
> 
> In **Desktop mode**, this is purely a UX gap. pgAdmin and the libpq it bundles share the same OS user, the same `~/.pgpass` is your own file, and auto-detecting it would just remove the unnecessary prompt. Defensible to fix.
> 
> In **Server mode**, it's a deliberate safety choice — and removing the prompt without guards would be a real security issue. pgAdmin in server mode runs as one shared OS user (often `pgadmin` on Linux, or `root` inside the `dpage/pgadmin` container), but **many distinct web users** log into it. If the server-process's `~/.pgpass` were auto-detected:
> 
> > *Admin puts `prod-db:5432:*:admin:secret` into the pgadmin user's `~/.pgpass` for their own use. Alice (a separate pgAdmin web user) registers a server pointing at `prod-db`, hits Connect. Without a prompt, the credentials silently flow through from the server's pgpass file. Alice now has access to credentials she was never granted.*
> 
> That's a privilege escalation, not just a noisy prompt. So in server mode, the conservative default (always prompt unless `passfile` is set per-server explicitly) is actually correct — the per-server `passfile` parameter exists precisely so an admin can deliberately scope credentials to a single server registration.
> 
> ## What we plan to do
> 
> A fix is sensible, but **gated on `config.SERVER_MODE == False`**:
> 
> - **Desktop mode**: detect the default `~/.pgpass` (and the Windows equivalent) at prompt-decision time, parse it for a matching `hostname:port:database:user:` entry, and skip the prompt if found. libpq will then transparently use the same file at connection time.
> - **Server mode**: no change. Auto-detection stays off. Admins continue to use the per-server `passfile` parameter for deliberate, scoped credential delegation.
> 
> There are a few subtleties to handle correctly — pgpass-format wildcards (`*:5432:*:postgres:secret`), backslash-escaped colons/backslashes in field values, file permissions (libpq refuses `~/.pgpass` if it's mode 0600 — pgAdmin's detector should check the same so we don't promise a path libpq will then reject). I'll work through them.
> 
> ## Workaround right now (works in both modes, today)
> 
> In pgAdmin: **Server Properties → Parameters → add an entry** with name `passfile` and value pointing at your pgpass file (the same path libpq uses). pgAdmin then skips the prompt for that specific server, matching the behavior the fix above will produce for the default location in desktop mode.
> 
> The path you'd use:
> 
> - Linux/Mac: `~/.pgpass` (resolved against the pgAdmin process's home dir — in desktop mode that's you; in server mode that's the pgAdmin user)
> - Windows: `%APPDATA%\postgresql\pgpass.conf`
> 
> Once you set that, the prompt should disappear immediately. **In server mode, please only use this for credentials you intend to share** — the file is on the server's filesystem, not yours.
> 
> Confirming desktop vs server will let me know whether the fix needs to gate on `SERVER_MODE == False` for your case, or whether the workaround is the right answer.

...

> Thanks all. Since 9.15 a user who does not own a shared server never inherits the owner's password file; it is a credential source and is treated like the owner's password or SSH key, so you are prompted instead. The server dialog documentation describes this. Each user can set their own *Password file* on their copy of the server, and the simplest way to give everyone the same file is to put it in a `SHARED_STORAGE` directory and reference it as `Name:/.pgpass`. Pressing OK with an empty password can still connect because libpq then falls back to the service account's own `.pgpass`, which is libpq's behaviour rather than pgAdmin's. Closing as by design; the broader discussion is in #10137.

 * Get a password from the password file. Return value is malloc'd.
 *
 * On failure, *errmsg is set to an error to be returned. It is
 * left NULL on success, or if no password could be found.
 */
static char *
passwordFromFile(const char *hostname, const char *port,
 const char *dbname, const char *username,
 const char *pgpassfile, const char **errmsg)
{
 FILE *fp;
#ifndef WIN32
 struct stat stat_buf;
#endif
 PQExpBufferData buf;

 *errmsg = NULL;

 if (dbname == NULL || dbname[0] == '\0')
 return NULL;

 if (username == NULL || username[0] == '\0')
 return NULL;

 /* 'localhost' matches pghost of '' or the default socket directory */
 if (hostname == NULL || hostname[0] == '\0')
 hostname = DefaultHost;
 else if (is_unixsock_path(hostname))

 /*
 * We should probably use canonicalize_path(), but then we have to
 * bring path.c into libpq, and it doesn't seem worth it.
 */
 if (strcmp(hostname, DEFAULT_PGSOCKET_DIR) == 0)
 hostname = DefaultHost;

 if (port == NULL || port[0] == '\0')
 port = DEF_PGPORT_STR;

 /* If password file cannot be opened, ignore it. */
 fp = fopen(pgpassfile, "r");
 if (fp == NULL)
 return NULL;

#ifndef WIN32
 if (fstat(fileno(fp), &stat_buf) != 0)
 {
 fclose(fp);
 return NULL;
 }

 if (!S_ISREG(stat_buf.st_mode))
 {
 fprintf(stderr,
 libpq_gettext("WARNING: password file \"%s\" is not a plain file\n"),
 pgpassfile);
 fclose(fp);
 return NULL;
 }

 /* If password file is insecure, alert the user and ignore it. */
 if (stat_buf.st_mode & (S_IRWXG | S_IRWXO))
 {
 fprintf(stderr,
 libpq_gettext("WARNING: password file \"%s\" has group or world access; permissions should be u=rw (0600) or less\n"),
 pgpassfile);
 fclose(fp);
 return NULL;
 }
#else

 /*
 * On Win32, the directory is protected, so we don't have to check the
 * file.
 */
#endif

 /* Use an expansible buffer to accommodate any reasonable line length */
 initPQExpBuffer(&buf);

 while (!feof(fp) && !ferror(fp))
 {
 /* Make sure there's a reasonable amount of room in the buffer */
 if (!enlargePQExpBuffer(&buf, 128))
 {
 *errmsg = libpq_gettext("out of memory");
 break;
 }

 /* Read some data, appending it to what we already have */
 if (fgets(buf.data + buf.len, buf.maxlen - buf.len, fp) == NULL)
 break;
 buf.len += strlen(buf.data + buf.len);

 /* If we don't yet have a whole line, loop around to read more */
 if (!(buf.len > 0 && buf.data[buf.len - 1] == '\n') && !feof(fp))
 continue;

 /* ignore comments */
 if (buf.data[0] != '#')
 {
 char *t = buf.data;
 int len;

 /* strip trailing newline and carriage return */
 len = pg_strip_crlf(t);

 if (len > 0 &&
 (t = pwdfMatchesString(t, hostname)) != NULL &&
 (t = pwdfMatchesString(t, port)) != NULL &&
 (t = pwdfMatchesString(t, dbname)) != NULL &&
 (t = pwdfMatchesString(t, username)) != NULL)
 {
 /* Found a match. */
 char *ret,
 *p1,
 *p2;

 ret = strdup(t);

 fclose(fp);
 explicit_bzero(buf.data, buf.maxlen);
 termPQExpBuffer(&buf);

 if (!ret)
 {
 *errmsg = libpq_gettext("out of memory");
 return NULL;
 }

 /* De-escape password. */
 for (p1 = p2 = ret; *p1 != ':' && *p1 != '\0'; ++p1, ++p2)
 {
 if (*p1 == '\\' && p1[1] != '\0')
 ++p1;
 *p2 = *p1;
 }
 *p2 = '\0';

 return ret;
 }
 }

 /* No match, reset buffer to prepare for next line. */
 buf.len = 0;
 }

 fclose(fp);
 explicit_bzero(buf.data, buf.maxlen);
 termPQExpBuffer(&buf);
 return NULL;
}

/*
 * If the connection failed due to bad password, we should mention
 * if we got the password from the pgpassfile.
 */
static void
pgpassfileWarning(PGconn *conn)
{
 /* If it was 'invalid authorization', add pgpassfile mention */
 /* only works with >= 9.0 servers */
 if (conn->password_needed &&
 conn->connhost[conn->whichhost].password != NULL &&
 conn->result)
 {
 const char *sqlstate = PQresultErrorField(conn->result,
 PG_DIAG_SQLSTATE);

 if (sqlstate && strcmp(sqlstate, ERRCODE_INVALID_PASSWORD) == 0)
 libpq_append_conn_error(conn, "password retrieved from file \"%s\"",
 conn->pgpassfile);
 }
}

/* Get a password from the password file. Return value is malloc'd. */
static char *
PasswordFromFile(char *hostname, char *port, char *dbname, char *username)
{
	FILE	   *fp;
	char		pgpassfile[MAXPGPATH];
	struct stat stat_buf;

#define LINELEN NAMEDATALEN*5
	char		buf[LINELEN];

	if (dbname == NULL || strlen(dbname) == 0)
		return NULL;

	if (username == NULL || strlen(username) == 0)
		return NULL;

	/* 'localhost' matches pghost of '' or the default socket directory */
	if (hostname == NULL)
		hostname = DefaultHost;
	else if (is_absolute_path(hostname))

		/*
		 * We should probably use canonicalize_path(), but then we have to
		 * bring path.c into libpq, and it doesn't seem worth it.
		 */
		if (strcmp(hostname, DEFAULT_PGSOCKET_DIR) == 0)
			hostname = DefaultHost;

	if (port == NULL)
		port = DEF_PGPORT_STR;

	if (!getPgPassFilename(pgpassfile))
		return NULL;

	/* If password file cannot be opened, ignore it. */
	if (stat(pgpassfile, &stat_buf) != 0)
		return NULL;

#ifndef WIN32
	if (!S_ISREG(stat_buf.st_mode))
	{
		fprintf(stderr,
		libpq_gettext("WARNING: password file \"%s\" is not a plain file\n"),
				pgpassfile);
		return NULL;
	}

	/* If password file is insecure, alert the user and ignore it. */
	if (stat_buf.st_mode & (S_IRWXG | S_IRWXO))
	{
		fprintf(stderr,
				libpq_gettext("WARNING: password file \"%s\" has group or world access; permissions should be u=rw (0600) or less\n"),
				pgpassfile);
		return NULL;
	}
#else

	/*
	 * On Win32, the directory is protected, so we don't have to check the
	 * file.
	 */
#endif

	fp = fopen(pgpassfile, "r");
	if (fp == NULL)
		return NULL;

	while (!feof(fp) && !ferror(fp))
	{
		char	   *t = buf,
				   *ret,
				   *p1,
				   *p2;
		int			len;

		if (fgets(buf, sizeof(buf), fp) == NULL)
			break;

		len = strlen(buf);

		/* Remove trailing newline */
		if (len > 0 && buf[len - 1] == '\n')
		{
			buf[--len] = '\0';
			/* Handle DOS-style line endings, too, even when not on Windows */
			if (len > 0 && buf[len - 1] == '\r')
				buf[--len] = '\0';
		}

		if (len == 0)
			continue;

		if ((t = pwdfMatchesString(t, hostname)) == NULL ||
			(t = pwdfMatchesString(t, port)) == NULL ||
			(t = pwdfMatchesString(t, dbname)) == NULL ||
			(t = pwdfMatchesString(t, username)) == NULL)
			continue;

		/* Found a match. */
		ret = strdup(t);
		fclose(fp);

		if (!ret)
		{
			/* Out of memory. XXX: an error message would be nice. */
			return NULL;
		}

		/* De-escape password. */
		for (p1 = p2 = ret; *p1 != ':' && *p1 != '\0'; ++p1, ++p2)
		{
			if (*p1 == '\\' && p1[1] != '\0')
				++p1;
			*p2 = *p1;
		}
		*p2 = '\0';

		return ret;
	}

	fclose(fp);
	return NULL;

#undef LINELEN
}

static bool
getPgPassFilename(char *pgpassfile)
{
	char	   *passfile_env;

	if ((passfile_env = getenv("PGPASSFILE")) != NULL)
		/* use the literal path from the environment, if set */
		strlcpy(pgpassfile, passfile_env, MAXPGPATH);
	else
	{
		char		homedir[MAXPGPATH];

		if (!pqGetHomeDirectory(homedir, sizeof(homedir)))
			return false;
		snprintf(pgpassfile, MAXPGPATH, "%s/%s", homedir, PGPASSFILE);
	}
	return true;
}

/*
 *	If the connection failed, we should mention if
 *	we got the password from .pgpass in case that
 *	password is wrong.
 */
static void
dot_pg_pass_warning(PGconn *conn)
{
	/* If it was 'invalid authorization', add .pgpass mention */
	/* only works with >= 9.0 servers */
	if (conn->dot_pgpass_used && conn->password_needed && conn->result &&
		strcmp(PQresultErrorField(conn->result, PG_DIAG_SQLSTATE),
			   ERRCODE_INVALID_PASSWORD) == 0)
	{
		char		pgpassfile[MAXPGPATH];

		if (!getPgPassFilename(pgpassfile))
			return;
		appendPQExpBuffer(&conn->errorMessage,
					  libpq_gettext("password retrieved from file \"%s\"\n"),
						  pgpassfile);
	}
}

If Mongo collection from a previous run exists, it compares old Mongo data vs new PG export → mismatches reported but script may still exit 0 (it doesn't fail on mismatches, just writes "No"). So U7 correctness isn't enforced. Real.

In `false && echo hi`, `false` is not the command following the final `&&` (that's echo), so failure is ignored; the list returns 1, but no exit. Yes. So no bug. D. **`ejecutar_segunda_entrega.sh:67` runs `configurar_auditoria.sql` without `ON_ERROR_STOP`**, so SQL errors (e.g., non-superuser, ALTER SYSTEM failure) don't stop the run; the evidence may show a partially configured audit. Also lines 123-124. Medium.

G. **`backup_foodstore.sh` + `restore_test.sh`: backups don't include roles/globals; restore test uses `--no-owner --no-privileges` and validates only 5 tables**, so DR test can't detect missing roles/grants/ownership and many tables. Medium.

K. **`roles.sql:128-135` hardcodes `FOR ROLE postgres` in `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES`**, so if run as another role/`PGUSER`, future objects don't get the intended policy. Low.

On Windows, the C runtime opened in text mode translates `\n` to `\r\n` on output. psql uses stdio; yes. The `restore_test.sh` explicitly handles it, confirming the project knows. So real.

Now, is `tr -d ' '` also problematic because it removes spaces inside JSON strings? IDs are numbers, so no. Fine.

Let me also double-check the `respaldo_tarea.cmd` errorlevel claim: In a batch file, after running the bash command, `%errorlevel%` on the next line reflects the exit code. But the batch file's own exit code is the exit code of the last command executed, which is `echo` → 0. Unless the batch reaches EOF, cmd sets errorlevel to the last command's. So yes. Also, `echo codigo de salida: %errorlevel%` — wait, `%errorlevel%` is expanded at parse time of the line, which is *before* executing the line but *after* the previous line completed. So it logs the bash exit code. But the script doesn't `exit /b %errorlevel%`. Confirmed.

Actually, there's a subtlety: `%errorlevel%` in a batch file line is expanded when the line is read, and cmd reads/parses line by line. So it should be the value after the bash command. Fine.

Now, is `cd %CD:\=/%` inside double quotes? The whole `-c` arg is double-quoted: `"cd %CD:\=/% && ./backup_foodstore.sh"`. Cmd expands `%CD:\=/%` to a forward-slash path. If the path contains spaces, the resulting bash command is `cd C:/Users/My Name/... && ./backup_foodstore.sh` — unquoted, so bash sees `cd` with two args: `C:/Users/My` and `Name/...` → "too many arguments". So breaks. Real. Verification: copy the folder to a path with a space and run the task. Or `schtasks /Run`.

Title: Echo command - Windows CMD
URL: https://ss64.com/nt/echo.html
Published: N/A
Author: N/A
Highlights:
# ECHO

Display messages on screen, turn command-echoing on or off.

```
Syntax
      ECHO [on | off] 
      ECHO [message]
      ECHO /?
      @ command
Key
   on      : Display each line of the batch on screen (default).
   off     : Only display the command output on screen.
   message : A string of characters to display.
   @       : Turn off ECHO for the current line only.
   /?      : Display help.
```

The on/off setting is not case sensitive. Type ECHO without parameters to display the current echo setting (ON or OFF).

At the command line turning Echo off will suppress display of the PROMPT.

In a batch file setting Echo off will suppress the display of all the batch commands leaving only the display output, turning Echo ON can be useful when debugging a problematic batch script.

In a batch file, the @ symbol at the start of a line is the same as ECHO OFF applied to the current line only.

Normally a command is executed and takes effect from the next line onwards, @ is a rare example of a command that takes effect immediately.

ECHO does not set or clear the Errorlevel. ECHO is an internal command.

## Echo text into a FILE

> The general syntax is: Echo This is some Text > FileName.txt
> 
> To avoid extra spaces: Echo Some more text> FileName.txt
> 
> An alternative (undocumented) syntax: > FileName.txt Echo Some more text
> 
> To create an empty (zero byte) file: Echo: 2> EmptyFile.txt
> 
> With all these commands, you may also want to append to an existing file using the >> redirection operator.

Title: Which cmd.exe internal commands clear the ERRORLEVEL to 0 upon success?
URL: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/34968009/which-cmd-exe-internal-commands-clear-the-errorlevel-to-0-upon-success
Published: N/A
Author: N/A
Highlights:
This answer is based on experiments I ran under Windows 10. I doubt there are differences with earlier Windows versions that use cmd.exe, but it is possible.

Also note - This answer does not attempt to document the ERRORLEVEL result when an internal command encounters an error (except for a wee bit concerning DEL and ERASE)

Not only are there difference between commands, but a single command can behave differently depending on whether it was run from the command line, or within a batch script with a .bat extension, or from within a batch script with a .cmd extension.

The following set of commands never clear the ERRORLEVEL to 0 upon success, regardless of context, but instead preserve the prior ERRORLEVEL:

BREAK
CLS
ECHO
ENDLOCAL
FOR : Obviously, commands in the DO clause may set the ERRORLEVEL, but a successful FOR with at least one iteration does not set the ERRORLEVEL to 0 on its own.
GOTO
IF : Obviously, commands executed by IF may set the ERRORLEVEL, but a successful IF does not set ERRORLEVEL to 0 on its own.
KEYS
PAUSE
POPD
RD
REM
RMDIR
SHIFT
START
TITLE

The next set of commands always clear the ERRORLEVEL to 0 upon success, regardless of context:

CD
CHDIR
COLOR
COPY
DATE
DEL : Always clears ERRORLEVEL, even if the DEL fails (except when run without any file argument).
DIR
ERASE : Always clears ERRORLEVEL, even if ERASE fails. (except when run without any file argument).
MD
MKDIR
MKLINK
MOVE
PUSHD
REN
RENAME
SETLOCAL
TIME
TYPE 
VER 
VERIFY 
VOL 

Then there are these commands that do not clear ERRORLEVEL upon success if issued from the command line or within a script with a .bat extension, but do clear the ERRORLEVEL to 0 if issued from a script with a .cmd extension. See https://stackoverflow.com/a/148991/1012053 and https://groups.google.com/forum/#!msg/microsoft.public.win2000.cmdprompt.admin/XHeUq8oe2wk/LIEViGNmkK0J for more info.

ASSOC
DPATH
FTYPE
PATH
PROMPT
SET

Lastly, there are these commands that do not fit neatly into any of the prior categories:

CALL : If a :routine or batch script is CALLed, then ERRORLEVEL is exclusively controlled by the CALLed script or :routine. But any other type of successful CALL to a command will always clear ERRORLEVEL to 0 if the CALLed command does not otherwise set it.
Example: call echo OK.
EXIT : If used without /B, then the cmd.exe session terminates and there is no more ERRORLEVEL, just the cmd.exe return code. Obviously EXIT /B 0 clears the ERRORLEVEL to 0, but EXIT /B without a value preserves the prior ERRORLEVEL.

I believe that accounts for all internal commands, unless there is an undocumented command that I missed.

...

Your description of CALL command is incomplete:

 CALL : Clears ERRORLEVEL if the CALLed command does not otherwise set it.
 Example: call echo OK.

Check this small example:

@echo off

call :setTwo
echo Set two: %errorlevel%

call :preserve
echo Preserve: %errorlevel%

call echo Reset
echo Reset: %errorlevel%

call :subNotExists 2> NUL
echo Sub not exist: %errorlevel%

goto :EOF

:setTwo
exit /B 2

:preserve
echo Preserve
exit /B

Output:

Set two: 2
Preserve
Preserve: 2
Reset
Reset: 0
Sub not exist: 1

CALL description should say something like this:

CALL : Clears ERRORLEVEL if the CALLed command does not otherwise set it. Example: call echo OK, but if the called command is a subroutine it preserves the prior ERRORLEVEL. If the called subroutine does not exist, it sets the ERRORLEVEL to 1.

Title: Resetting ERRORLEVEL in batch scripts
URL: https://groups.google.com/g/comp.os.msdos.programmer/c/02zLyiL8xgU
Published: 1998-07-14T00:00:00.000Z
Author: N/A
Highlights:
This is normal. It's an internal variable. I don't know any method to reset it to zero. You could try to write a program that terminates with errorlevel 0. But that should not be necessary. Why do you ask for the errorlevel value twice? You can ask for it thousands of times in your batch, but always preceded by a program that returns a termination code. It seems somewhat weird to me that the fact that the value remains unchanged disturbs the execution of your batch...

...

If I write a script as follows:

@echo off if ERRORLEVEL 1 goto err echo I'm OK goto :eof

:err echo Failed

Then I run this it prints I'm OK

Next I type: junk which fails after which whenever I run the script it prints Failed.

It occurs to me as I write this that maybe all the commands such as echo, set, if, call (my real script is obviously more complex than the above) are maybe not treated the same as running a program and thus don't set the ERRORLEVEL.

I'd assumed that things like echo, if and call would reset the ERRORLEVEL since they succeed. I'll try your suggestion of calling some small program which sets error code to 0 and see if that works.

...

You have a *serious* misunderstanding of what ERRORLEVEL is - it's the return value from an EXE or COM program that terminates with INT 21, function 4C. Any other means of termination returns a zero. Internal commands (those that are part of the command interpreter rather than external files) *cannot* change ERRORLEVEL because they don't terminate in the usual sense - they are in the nature of subroutines inside the command processor that is interpreting the script.

...

The errorlevel is a return value from EXTERNAL programs. INTERNAL commands (such as echo and set) do not return values. Although there would be some use for errorlevel as a means of obtaining an error code from the last operating system command it is generally unncessary (e.g., what use would an error code for "echo" be?).

As previously pointed out, it is also unusual to use errorlevel without explicitly running a program right before it.

However, it can be set to zero with a very simple program. One way to create such a program is by using a DEBUG:

debug < debug.scr

where debug.scr (.scr is for script) is as follows (to produce a program named " CERROR.COM", for clear-errorlevel):

--DEBUG.SCR - cut here---- n cerror.com a mov ax,4c00 int 21

r bx 0 r cx 5 w q --DEBUG.SCR - cut here---

Note that the blank line after the "int 21" is necessary.

Title: Batch file - How to combine multiple echo statements and also reset %errorlevel% on a single line?
URL: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/22844457/batch-file-how-to-combine-multiple-echo-statements-and-also-reset-errorlevel
Published: 2014-04-03T17:10:37.000Z
Author: user3494797
Highlights:
```
@echo off
setlocal EnableDelayedExpansion

set /P "=ERRORLEVEL has been reset from %errorlevel% to " < NUL & verify>nul & echo !errorlevel!
```

...

The reason why your code does not show two different values for %ErrorLevel% is because the environment variable is substituted in the entire command line before any command is run. Only then is the command line executed. But you need the second substitution to occur after the _ver_ command has run.

First of all, you could take advantage of delayed expansion, in which environment variables surrounded by exclamation marks are expanded only when the command is about to be run. To turn on this mode, you need to execute **SETLOCAL ENABLEDELAYEDEXPANSION**

```
SETLOCAL ENABLEDELAYEDEXPANSION

ECHO ERRORLEVEL has been reset from !ERRORLEVEL! to & verify>nul & ECHO !ERRORLEVEL!
```

(By the way Delayed Expansion only appears to work in batch files, not at the command line).

Unfortunately, there is no way of preventing the new line from being shown by the ECHO command. So instead, you are forced to do each command on a single line. But fear not, you just need to save all the values you need, and do all the output on a single line.

So your code should be:

```
@ECHO OFF
SET OriginalErrorLevel=%ERRORLEVEL%
verify>nul
SET NewErrorLevel=%ERRORLEVEL%
ECHO ERRORLEVEL has been reset from %OriginalErrorLevel% to %NewErrorLevel%
```

Incidentally, don't bother prefixing every command with "@". Just use **@ECHO OFF** at the top of every script, and no commands will be shown unless you subsequently use **ECHO ON**.

...

```
@echo off

...

call :seterr 4
verify>nul&echo ERRORLEVEL has been reset from %errorlevel% to !errorlevel!

GOTO :EOF

:seterr
exit /b %1
```

This exploits the normal parsing characteristic where `%errorlevel%` will be replaced by the actual errorlevel at the time of parsing - before execution. `!errorlevel! **WILL** be resolved to the runtime-value of`errorlevel`if`delayedexpansion\` has been invoked.

Note that you should not assign a value to `errorlevel`. It is a `"magic variable"` - established by the system, but will be overridden by a setting explicitly made by the user. Other variables in this category are `time`, `date` and `cd`, amongst others.

Title: What is the easiest way to reset ERRORLEVEL to zero?
URL: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/1113727/what-is-the-easiest-way-to-reset-errorlevel-to-zero
Published: N/A
Author: N/A
Highlights:
I found that "exit 0" looks like a good way to deal with this problem.

Usage Example:

 NET STOP UnderDevService /Y
 
 exit 0

if the UnderDevService service is not started.

### Answer by akf (score: 78)

if you use exit /b 0 you can return an errorlevel 0 from within a child batch script without also exiting the parent. 

### Answer by Jason Kresowaty (score: 63)

Seems to do the trick:

ver > nul

Not everything works, and it is not clear why. For example, the following do not:

echo. > nul
cls > nul

### Answer by Jeffrey Wilges (score: 37)

In a pre- or post-build event, if the return code of an executable is greater than zero, and the call to the executable is not the last line of the pre- or post-build event, a quick way to mute it and avoid triggering a check for a non-zero errorlevel is to follow the failing line with a line that explicitly returns zero:
cmd /c "exit /b 0"

This is essentially a generic combination of the previously-mentioned solutions that will work with more than just the last line of a pre- or post-build event.

...

If this is a snippet like "Post-build Event" etc., then you'll be fine appending:

(...) || ver > nul

at the end of the last command.

Alternatively

cmd /c "exit /b 0"

is very clean and non-idiomatic -- a reader who knows Windows shell will know what's going on, and what was your intent.

However, if you're in a batch script, you may want to use subrotines, which are a lightweight equivalent of the "child batch script" from akf's answer.

Have a subroutine:

:reset_error
exit /b 0

and then just

call :reset_error

wherever you need it.

Here's a complete example:

@echo off
rem *** main ***

call :raise_error
echo After :raise_error ERRORLEVEL = %ERRORLEVEL%

call :empty
echo After :empty ERRORLEVEL = %ERRORLEVEL%

call :reset_error
echo After :reset_error ERRORLEVEL = %ERRORLEVEL%

:: this is needed at the end of the main body of the script
goto:eof

rem *** subroutines ***

:empty
goto:eof

:raise_error
exit /b 1

:reset_error
exit /b 0

Which outputs:

After :raise_error ERRORLEVEL = 1
After :empty ERRORLEVEL = 1
After :reset_error ERRORLEVEL = 0

As you see - just calling and returning via goto:eof is not enough.

Title: Batch files - Errorlevels
URL: https://www.robvanderwoude.com/errorlevel.php
Published: N/A
Author: N/A
Highlights:
Errorlevels are not a standard feature of every command. A certain errorlevel may mean anything the programmer wanted it to. Most programmers agree that an errorlevel 0 means the command executed successfully, and an errorlevel 1 or higher usually spells trouble. But there are many exceptions to this general rule.

`IF ERRORLEVEL` construction has one strange feature, that can be used to our advantage: it returns TRUE if the return code was equal to or higher than the specified errorlevel.

This means most of the time we only need to check `IF ERRORLEVEL 1 ...` and this will return TRUE for every positive, non-zero return code. Likewise, `IF NOT ERRORLEVEL 0 ...` will return TRUE for every negative, non-zero return code.

...

| In Windows NT 4 (and 2000?) this won't work, since the SET command itself will set an errorlevel (usually 0)! (As I learned from Charles Long, in XP the SET command no longer sets an errorlevel itself.) However, Windows NT 4 and later make it easy by storing the latest errorlevel in the environment variable ERRORLEVEL: `ECHO.%ERRORLEVEL%` will display the errorlevel. This blog entry by Batcheero explains perfectly why you should never SET the ERRORLEVEL variable. The safest way to use errorlevels for all DOS versions is the reverse order check. Start checking the highest errorlevel

...

IF ERRORLEVEL 254 GOTO Label254

...

To check errorlevels during batch file development, use either COMMAND /Z yourbatch.bat to display the errorlevel of every command executed in MS-DOS 7.* (Windows 95/98), or PROMPT Errorlevel$Q$R$_$P$G in OS/2 Warp (DOS) sessions.

...

Use ERRORLVL.EXE from OzWoz Software, or SETERLEV.COM 1.0 from Jim Elliott to test batch files that (are supposed to) check on errorlevels. The syntax couldn't be simpler:

`ERRORLVL number`

or

`SETERLEV number`

where number can be any number from 0 to 255.

...

## Windows 2000 and later:

In Windows 2000 and later the `EXIT` command accepts an optional exit code, a.k.a. return code or errorlevel, e.g. `EXIT /B 1` for errorlevel 1:

### EXIT

Quits the CMD.EXE program (command interpreter) or the current batch script.

`EXIT  [ /B ]  [ exitCode ]`

| /B | Specifies to exit the current batch script instead of CMD.EXE. If executed from outside a batch script, it will quit CMD.EXE. |
| --- | --- |
| exitCode | Specifies a numeric number. If /B is specified, sets ERRORLEVEL that number. If quitting CMD.EXE, sets the process exit code with that number. |

[ Brought to my attention by Maor Conforti. Thanks ]

If you want to set an errorlevel inside a batch file, for example to test an external command used by that batch file, you can use `CMD.EXE /D /K EXIT 6` to set errorlevel 6 and continue. `CMD`'s `/D` switch disables any command processor AutoRun commands you may have set on your computer (you can check this by looking for `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Microsoft\Command Processor\AutoRun` in the registry). Do NOT use `SET ErrorLevel=6` as this will render the `Errorlevel` variable static (`SET ErrorLevel=` will restore it to a dynamic variable again).
```

4: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION fn_total_pedido(p_id_pedido BIGINT)
5: RETURNS NUMERIC(14,2)
6: LANGUAGE plpgsql
7: STABLE
8: AS $$
9: DECLARE
10:     v_total NUMERIC(14,2);
11: BEGIN
12:     SELECT COALESCE(SUM(dp.cantidad * dp.precio_unitario), 0)
13:       INTO v_total
14:       FROM detalle_pedido dp
15:      WHERE dp.id_pedido = p_id_pedido;
16: 
17:     RETURN v_total;
18: END;
19: $$;
20: 
21: -- 6.2 PROCEDIMIENTO: registrar un pedido completo
22: CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE sp_registrar_pedido(
23:     p_id_cliente  BIGINT,
24:     p_forma_pago  forma_pago_enum,
25:     p_items       JSONB
26: )
27: LANGUAGE plpgsql
28: AS $$
29: DECLARE
30:     v_id_pedido BIGINT;
31:     v_item      JSONB;
32: BEGIN
33:     IF p_items IS NULL OR jsonb_array_length(p_items) = 0 THEN
34:         RAISE EXCEPTION 'El pedido debe tener al menos un ítem';
35:     END IF;
36: 
37:     INSERT INTO pedido (forma_pago, id_cliente)
38:     VALUES (p_forma_pago, p_id_cliente)
39:     RETURNING id_pedido INTO v_id_pedido;
40: 
41:     FOR v_item IN SELECT * FROM jsonb_array_elements(p_items) LOOP
42:         -- La línea se inserta con el precio de lista vigente.
43:         INSERT INTO detalle_pedido (cantidad, precio_unitario, id_pedido, id_producto)
44:         SELECT (v_item->>'cantidad')::INT, pr.precio, v_id_pedido, pr.id_producto
45:           FROM producto pr
46:          WHERE pr.id_producto = (v_item->>'id_producto')::BIGINT;
47: 
48:         IF NOT FOUND THEN
49:             RAISE EXCEPTION 'Producto % inexistente', v_item->>'id_producto';
50:         END IF;
51: 
52:         UPDATE producto
53:            SET stock = stock - (v_item->>'cantidad')::INT
54:          WHERE id_producto = (v_item->>'id_producto')::BIGINT;
55:     END LOOP;
56: 
57:     RAISE NOTICE 'Pedido % registrado. Total: %', v_id_pedido, fn_total_pedido(v_id_pedido);
58: END;
59: $$;

7: --   * SET search_path fijo: evita que alguien cree un objeto con el mismo nombre en otro
8: --     esquema y la función lo use (ataque clásico a funciones SECURITY DEFINER).
9: --   * Cada intento queda en auditoria_seguridad (registro de rendición de cuentas) y,
10: --     además, en el log del servidor con RAISE LOG (registro técnico).
11: --   * EXECUTE se revoca de PUBLIC: por defecto, cualquier rol puede ejecutar una función.
12: --   * SET log_min_error_statement = 'panic': para el log del servidor, el nivel LOG está por
13: --     encima de ERROR, así que cada RAISE LOG agregaba la línea STATEMENT con la llamada
14: --     completa, es decir, con la contraseña en texto plano. Se detectó al probar el
15: --     simulacro (ver BITACORA.md). Con este ajuste, solo dentro de estas funciones, el log
16: --     registra el evento sin la sentencia.
17: 
18: CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pgcrypto;
19: 
20: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS auditoria_seguridad (
21:     id          BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
22:     momento     TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT clock_timestamp(),
23:     evento      TEXT        NOT NULL CHECK (evento IN ('LOGIN', 'RESET_PASSWORD')),
24:     exito       BOOLEAN     NOT NULL,
25:     mail        TEXT        NOT NULL,
26:     usuario_id  BIGINT,
27:     rol_bd      TEXT        NOT NULL DEFAULT session_user,
28:     origen      INET                 DEFAULT inet_client_addr()
29: );
30: 
31: -- Devuelve el usuario si el mail y la contraseña coinciden; si no, ninguna fila.
32: -- No distingue "mail inexistente" de "contraseña incorrecta" para no revelar qué mails existen.
33: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION fn_autenticar(p_mail TEXT, p_contrasena TEXT)
34: RETURNS TABLE (usuario_id BIGINT, nombre TEXT, rol TEXT)
35: LANGUAGE plpgsql
36: SECURITY DEFINER
37: SET search_path = public, pg_temp
38: SET log_min_error_statement = 'panic'
39: AS $$
40: DECLARE
41:     v_id     BIGINT;
42:     v_nombre TEXT;
43:     v_rol    TEXT;
44:     v_hash   TEXT;
45: BEGIN
46:     SELECT u.id, u.nombre, u.rol::TEXT, u.contrasena
47:       INTO v_id, v_nombre, v_rol, v_hash
48:       FROM usuario u
49:      WHERE lower(u.mail) = lower(p_mail) AND NOT u.eliminado;
50: 
51:     -- Solo se comparan hashes bcrypt; las contraseñas heredadas en otro formato no validan.
52:     IF v_hash LIKE '$2%' AND crypt(p_contrasena, v_hash) = v_hash THEN
53:         INSERT INTO auditoria_seguridad (evento, exito, mail, usuario_id)
54:         VALUES ('LOGIN', TRUE, p_mail, v_id);
55:         RAISE LOG 'fn_autenticar: inicio de sesion correcto mail=% usuario_id=%', p_mail, v_id;
56:         RETURN QUERY SELECT v_id, v_nombre, v_rol;
57:     ELSE
58:         INSERT INTO auditoria_seguridad (evento, exito, mail, usuario_id)
59:         VALUES ('LOGIN', FALSE, p_mail, v_id);
60:         RAISE LOG 'fn_autenticar: intento fallido mail=%', p_mail;
61:     END IF;
62: END $$;
63: 
64: -- Reemplaza la contraseña de un usuario. Reservada a soporte.
65: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION fn_resetear_password(p_mail TEXT, p_nueva TEXT)
66: RETURNS BOOLEAN
67: LANGUAGE plpgsql
68: SECURITY DEFINER
69: SET search_path = public, pg_temp
70: SET log_min_error_statement = 'panic'
71: AS $$
72: DECLARE
73:     v_id BIGINT;
74: BEGIN
75:     IF length(p_nueva) < 10 THEN
76:         RAISE EXCEPTION 'La contraseña nueva debe tener al menos 10 caracteres';
77:     END IF;
78: 
79:     UPDATE usuario
80:        SET contrasena = crypt(p_nueva, gen_salt('bf', 10))
81:      WHERE lower(mail) = lower(p_mail) AND NOT eliminado
82:     RETURNING id INTO v_id;
83: 
84:     INSERT INTO auditoria_seguridad (evento, exito, mail, usuario_id)
85:     VALUES ('RESET_PASSWORD', v_id IS NOT NULL, p_mail, v_id);
86:     RAISE LOG 'fn_resetear_password: mail=% exito=%', p_mail, v_id IS NOT NULL;
87:     RETURN v_id IS NOT NULL;
88: END $$;
89: 
90: REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION fn_autenticar(TEXT, TEXT)        FROM PUBLIC;
91: REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION fn_resetear_password(TEXT, TEXT) FROM PUBLIC;
92: 
93: -- Funciones de trigger que escriben tablas internas (auditoría de precios de la U3 y
94: -- resumen de ventas de la U4). Si corrieran con los permisos de quien vende, habría que
95: -- darle a app_web permiso de escritura sobre esas tablas. Corriendo como dueño, no.
96: ALTER FUNCTION fn_auditar_precios()          SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp;
97: ALTER FUNCTION fn_resumen_detalle()          SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp;
98: ALTER FUNCTION fn_resumen_cambio_categoria() SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp;

</content>

1: -- U5 · roles.sql — Roles y permisos de Food Store con mínimo privilegio
2: --
3: -- Se ejecuta como postgres sobre la base del proyecto y se puede repetir: los roles se
4: -- crean si no existen y, antes de otorgar, se revoca todo lo anterior. Así, el resultado
5: -- es siempre exactamente lo que dice este archivo.
6: --
7: -- Las contraseñas NO se escriben acá. Después de correrlo, en psql:
8: --   \password app_web       \password admin_datos
9: --   \password usr_soporte   \password usr_reportes   \password usr_auditor
10: --
11: -- Justificación de cada rol (una oración cada uno):
12: --   rol_app_lectura   La tienda web muestra el catálogo y los pedidos: lee categorías, productos y pedidos, y nada con datos personales.
13: --   rol_app_escritura La tienda web registra ventas: inserta pedidos y sus líneas y descuenta stock, sin poder cambiar precios.
14: --   rol_soporte       La mesa de ayuda atiende a usuarios y clientes: los consulta sin ver contraseñas, corrige el celular o la baja, y resetea contraseñas solo con la función.
15: --   rol_reportes      El área comercial mira resultados agregados: lee vistas de ventas y la tabla anonimizada de usuarios, nunca datos personales.
16: --   rol_auditor       (adicional) Quien investiga un incidente lee los registros de auditoría, y ningún dato del negocio.
17: --   app_web           Login de la aplicación: lectura + escritura de la tienda y la función de autenticación.
18: --   admin_datos       Login del administrador de datos: todo sobre las tablas del esquema salvo modificar la auditoría, sin ser superusuario ni poder crear roles.
19: --   usr_soporte, usr_reportes, usr_auditor  (adicionales) Logins personales de cada área, para que el log diga quién hizo qué.
20: 
21: \set ON_ERROR_STOP on
22: 
23: -- 1. Crear los roles si no existen ------------------------------------------------
24: DO $$
25: DECLARE
26:     r TEXT;
27: BEGIN
28:     FOREACH r IN ARRAY ARRAY['rol_app_lectura', 'rol_app_escritura', 'rol_soporte', 'rol_reportes', 'rol_auditor'] LOOP
29:         IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = r) THEN
30:             EXECUTE format('CREATE ROLE %I NOLOGIN', r);
31:         END IF;
32:     END LOOP;
33:     FOREACH r IN ARRAY ARRAY['app_web', 'admin_datos', 'usr_soporte', 'usr_reportes', 'usr_auditor'] LOOP
34:         IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = r) THEN
35:             EXECUTE format('CREATE ROLE %I LOGIN', r);
36:         END IF;
37:     END LOOP;
38: END $$;
39: 
40: -- Ningún rol es superusuario ni puede crear roles o bases.
41: ALTER ROLE app_web      NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE NOBYPASSRLS CONNECTION LIMIT 20;
42: ALTER ROLE admin_datos  NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE NOBYPASSRLS CONNECTION LIMIT 3;
43: ALTER ROLE usr_soporte  NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE NOBYPASSRLS CONNECTION LIMIT 5;
44: ALTER ROLE usr_reportes NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE NOBYPASSRLS CONNECTION LIMIT 5;
45: ALTER ROLE usr_auditor  NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE NOBYPASSRLS CONNECTION LIMIT 2;
46: 
47: -- 2. Punto de partida limpio -------------------------------------------------------
48: DO $$
49: DECLARE
50:     r TEXT;
51: BEGIN
52:     FOREACH r IN ARRAY ARRAY['rol_app_lectura', 'rol_app_escritura', 'rol_soporte', 'rol_reportes', 'rol_auditor',
53:                              'app_web', 'admin_datos', 'usr_soporte', 'usr_reportes', 'usr_auditor'] LOOP
54:         EXECUTE format('REVOKE ALL ON ALL TABLES    IN SCHEMA public FROM %I', r);
55:         EXECUTE format('REVOKE ALL ON ALL SEQUENCES IN SCHEMA public FROM %I', r);
56:         EXECUTE format('REVOKE ALL ON ALL ROUTINES  IN SCHEMA public FROM %I', r);
57:         EXECUTE format('REVOKE ALL ON SCHEMA public FROM %I', r);
58:         EXECUTE format('REVOKE ALL ON DATABASE %I FROM %I', current_database(), r);
59:     END LOOP;
60:     -- Los permisos de columna no se van con REVOKE ALL ON ALL TABLES.
61:     EXECUTE 'REVOKE ALL (id, nombre, apellido, mail, celular, contrasena, rol, eliminado, created_at) ON usuario FROM rol_soporte';
62:     EXECUTE 'REVOKE ALL (stock) ON producto FROM rol_app_escritura';
63: END $$;

65: -- PUBLIC (todos los roles) no se conecta, no usa el esquema y no ejecuta funciones nuevas.
66: DO $$ BEGIN EXECUTE format('REVOKE ALL ON DATABASE %I FROM PUBLIC', current_database()); END $$;
67: REVOKE ALL ON SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC;
68: REVOKE EXECUTE ON ALL ROUTINES IN SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC;
69: 
70: -- 3. Conexión y esquema ------------------------------------------------------------

106: GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION fn_autenticar(TEXT, TEXT) TO app_web;     -- solo la app autentica

109: GRANT rol_reportes TO usr_reportes;

113: -- TRIGGER, no es dueño de los objetos y no tiene ADMIN OPTION sobre ningún rol.

1: """Extrae del log del servidor el fragmento entre dos marcas.
2: 
3: Uso: python extraer_log.py MARCA
4: Lee el archivo de log actual con pg_read_binary_file (hace falta conectarse como postgres)
5: y devuelve las líneas desde 'MARCA INICIO <marca>' hasta 'MARCA FIN <marca>'.
6: Se lee en binario porque, en Windows con idioma español, el log puede estar en WIN1252.
7: """
8: import base64
9: import os
10: import subprocess
11: import sys
12: 
13: 
14: def main() -> int:
15:     if len(sys.argv) != 2:
16:         print("Uso: python extraer_log.py MARCA", file=sys.stderr)
17:         return 2
18:     marca = sys.argv[1]
19:     db = os.environ.get("DB", "foodstore")
20:     consulta = "SELECT encode(pg_read_binary_file(pg_current_logfile()), 'base64')"
21:     salida = subprocess.run(["psql", "-d", db, "-X", "-At", "-c", consulta],
22:                             capture_output=True, check=True).stdout
23:     datos = b"".join(salida.split())
24:     if not datos:
25:         print("No hay archivo de log: logging_collector está apagado (ver PASOS.md).", file=sys.stderr)
26:         return 1
27:     crudo = base64.b64decode(datos)
28:     try:
29:         texto = crudo.decode("utf-8")
30:     except UnicodeDecodeError:
31:         texto = crudo.decode("cp1252", errors="replace")
32: 
33:     lineas = texto.splitlines()
34:     inicio = next((i for i, l in enumerate(lineas) if f"MARCA INICIO {marca}" in l), None)
35:     fin = next((i for i, l in enumerate(lineas) if f"MARCA FIN {marca}" in l), None)
36:     if inicio is None or fin is None:
37:         print(f"No se encontraron las marcas de {marca} en el log actual.", file=sys.stderr)
38:         return 1
39:     sys.stdout.write("\n".join(lineas[inicio:fin + 1]) + "\n")
40:     return 0
41: 
42: 
43: if __name__ == "__main__":

<path>C:\Users\moran\BD2\tpi-food-store\trabajos-practicos\unidad5_seguridad\scripts\anonimizar_log.py</path>
<type>file</type>
<content>
1: """Anonimiza un fragmento de log antes de dárselo a un asistente de IA.
2: 
3: Uso: python anonimizar_log.py < log_original.txt > log_anonimizado.txt
4: 
5: Criterio, el mismo de sql/usuario_anon.sql:
6:   * mails      -> 'anon_' + 10 caracteres de sha256('foodstore-u5:' + mail) + '@ejemplo.test'
7:   * IP y puerto de origen -> ip_origen_N (la misma IP recibe siempre el mismo N)
8:   * contraseñas pasadas como argumento a fn_autenticar o fn_resetear_password -> '***'
9: Los nombres de roles de base (app_web, admin_datos) no son datos personales y se conservan.
10: """
11: import hashlib
12: import re
13: import sys
14: 
15: SAL = "foodstore-u5:"
16: MAIL = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}")
17: # IPv4 o IPv6 seguidas de "(puerto)", como las escribe %r en log_line_prefix
18: IP_CON_PUERTO = re.compile(r"(?<![\w.:])((?:\d{1,3}\.){3}\d{1,3}|[0-9A-Fa-f]{0,4}(?::[0-9A-Fa-f]{0,4}){2,7})\((\d+)\)")
19: # "host=... port=..." de la línea "connection received"
20: HOST = re.compile(r"host=((?:\d{1,3}\.){3}\d{1,3}|[0-9A-Fa-f:]+)")
21: PUERTO = re.compile(r"port=\d+")
22: CLAVE = re.compile(r"((?:fn_autenticar|fn_resetear_password)\(\s*'[^']*'\s*,\s*)'[^']*'")
23: 
24: ips: dict[str, str] = {}
25: 
26: 
27: def alias_ip(ip: str) -> str:
28:     if ip not in ips:
29:         ips[ip] = f"ip_origen_{len(ips) + 1}"
30:     return ips[ip]
31: 
32: 
33: def alias_mail(m: re.Match) -> str:
34:     h = hashlib.sha256((SAL + m.group(0).lower()).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
35:     return f"anon_{h[:10]}@ejemplo.test"
36: 
37: 
38: def anonimizar(linea: str) -> str:
39:     linea = CLAVE.sub(r"\1'***'", linea)
40:     linea = MAIL.sub(alias_mail, linea)
41:     linea = IP_CON_PUERTO.sub(lambda m: f"{alias_ip(m.group(1))}(puerto)", linea)
42:     linea = HOST.sub(lambda m: f"host={alias_ip(m.group(1))}", linea)
43:     linea = PUERTO.sub("port=(puerto)", linea)
44:     return linea
45: 
46: 
47: def main() -> None:
48:     for linea in sys.stdin:
49:         sys.stdout.write(anonimizar(linea))
50: 
51: 
52: if __name__ == "__main__":
53:     main()

1: #!/usr/bin/env bash
2: # U6 — Respaldo de foodstore en formato custom.
3: # Uso: ./backup_foodstore.sh   (variables opcionales: PGHOST, PGPORT, PGUSER, DB)
4: # La contraseña NO va acá: se toma de pgpass.conf.
5: set -euo pipefail
6: cd "$(dirname "$0")"
7: 
8: DB="${DB:-foodstore}"
9: export PGHOST="${PGHOST:-localhost}" PGPORT="${PGPORT:-5432}" PGUSER="${PGUSER:-postgres}"
10: mkdir -p backups logs
11: 
12: marca="$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)"
13: dump="backups/${DB}_${marca}.dump"
14: conteos="backups/${DB}_${marca}.conteos.txt"
15: log="logs/backup.log"
16: 
17: registrar() { echo "$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') $*" | tee -a "$log"; }
18: 
19: registrar "INICIO respaldo de $DB en $PGHOST:$PGPORT -> $dump"
20: 
21: # Filas por tabla en el momento del respaldo: la restauración de prueba las compara.
22: if ! psql -X -d "$DB" -At -F ' ' -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -c "
23:     SELECT 'categoria', COUNT(*) FROM categoria
24:     UNION ALL SELECT 'cliente', COUNT(*) FROM cliente
25:     UNION ALL SELECT 'producto', COUNT(*) FROM producto
26:     UNION ALL SELECT 'pedido', COUNT(*) FROM pedido
27:     UNION ALL SELECT 'detalle_pedido', COUNT(*) FROM detalle_pedido;" > "$conteos"; then
28:     registrar "ERROR no se pudo conectar a $DB para contar filas"
29:     exit 1
30: fi
31: 
32: inicio=$(date +%s)
33: if ! pg_dump -d "$DB" -Fc -f "$dump" 2>> "$log"; then
34:     registrar "ERROR pg_dump falló (ver líneas anteriores de $log)"
35:     rm -f "$dump"
36:     exit 1
37: fi
38: fin=$(date +%s)
39: 
40: # El archivo tiene que poder leerse: si pg_restore no puede listarlo, el respaldo no sirve.
41: if ! objetos=$(pg_restore --list "$dump" 2>> "$log" | grep -vc '^;'); then
42:     registrar "ERROR el archivo $dump no se puede leer con pg_restore"
43:     exit 1
44: fi
45: 
46: tamano=$(du -h "$dump" | cut -f1)
47: registrar "OK $dump  tamaño=$tamano  objetos=$objetos  duración=$((fin - inicio))s"

1: #!/usr/bin/env bash
2: # U6 — Simulacro de desastre contra reloj: restaura el último respaldo en
3: # foodstore_restore_test, valida y mide RTO y RPO.
4: # La base principal no se toca. La contraseña sale de pgpass.conf.
5: # JOBS=4 ./restore_test.sh restaura en paralelo (mejora propuesta en el informe).
6: set -euo pipefail
7: cd "$(dirname "$0")"
8: 
9: ORIGEN="${DB:-foodstore}"
10: DESTINO="foodstore_restore_test"
11: export PGHOST="${PGHOST:-localhost}" PGPORT="${PGPORT:-5432}" PGUSER="${PGUSER:-postgres}"
12: mkdir -p logs evidencias
13: 
14: if [ "$DESTINO" = "$ORIGEN" ]; then echo "El destino no puede ser la base principal" >&2; exit 1; fi
15: 
16: dump="$(ls -t backups/"${ORIGEN}"_*.dump 2>/dev/null | head -1 || true)"
17: if [ -z "$dump" ]; then echo "No hay respaldos en backups/. Corré antes ./backup_foodstore.sh" >&2; exit 1; fi
18: conteos="${dump%.dump}.conteos.txt"
19: 
20: # Fecha del respaldo, tomada del nombre del archivo (AAAAMMDD_HHMMSS)
21: sello="$(basename "$dump" .dump)"; sello="${sello#"${ORIGEN}"_}"
22: fecha_respaldo="${sello:0:4}-${sello:4:2}-${sello:6:2} ${sello:9:2}:${sello:11:2}:${sello:13:2}"
23: reporte="evidencias/restore_test_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S).txt"
24: 
25: {
26: echo "Simulacro de restauración de $ORIGEN"
27: echo "Respaldo usado:        $dump"
28: echo "Fecha del respaldo:    $fecha_respaldo"
29: echo "Tamaño del respaldo:   $(du -h "$dump" | cut -f1)"
30: echo "Restauración en paralelo: ${JOBS:-no (1 proceso)}"
31: echo
32: 
33: # Preparación (fuera del cronómetro): si quedó una base de prueba de un simulacro anterior, se borra.
34: dropdb --if-exists "$DESTINO"
35: 
36: echo "== Cronómetro: INICIO $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')"
37: t0=$(date +%s%N)
38: 
39: createdb "$DESTINO"
40: pg_restore -d "$DESTINO" --no-owner --no-privileges --exit-on-error ${JOBS:+--jobs="$JOBS"} "$dump"
41: t_restore=$(date +%s%N)
42: 
43: echo
44: echo "== Validación 1: filas por tabla (respaldo vs restaurada)"
45: psql -X -d "$DESTINO" -At -F ' ' -c "
46:     SELECT 'categoria', COUNT(*) FROM categoria
47:     UNION ALL SELECT 'cliente', COUNT(*) FROM cliente
48:     UNION ALL SELECT 'producto', COUNT(*) FROM producto
49:     UNION ALL SELECT 'pedido', COUNT(*) FROM pedido
50:     UNION ALL SELECT 'detalle_pedido', COUNT(*) FROM detalle_pedido;" > /tmp/conteos_restaurada.txt
51: printf "%-16s %12s %12s %s\n" tabla respaldo restaurada coincide
52: ok_filas=1
53: # psql en Windows termina las líneas con \r\n: se quita el \r antes de comparar.
54: while read -r tabla n_resp; do
55:     n_resp="${n_resp//$'\r'/}"
56:     n_rest=$(awk -v t="$tabla" '$1 == t {print $2}' /tmp/conteos_restaurada.txt | tr -d '\r')
57:     if [ "$n_resp" = "$n_rest" ]; then c="sí"; else c="NO"; ok_filas=0; fi
58:     printf "%-16s %12s %12s %s\n" "$tabla" "$n_resp" "$n_rest" "$c"
59: done < "$conteos"
60: 
61: echo
62: echo "== Validación 2: restricciones lógicas (se espera 0 y 0)"
63: invalidos=$(psql -X -d "$DESTINO" -At -F ' ' -c "
64:     SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM producto WHERE precio < 0 OR stock < 0),
65:            (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM detalle_pedido WHERE cantidad <= 0 OR precio_unitario < 0);" | tr -d '\r')
66: echo "productos_invalidos detalles_invalidos"
67: echo "$invalidos"
68: 
69: t1=$(date +%s%N)
70: echo
71: echo "== Cronómetro: FIN $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')"
72: 
73: rto_ms=$(( (t1 - t0) / 1000000 ))
74: restore_ms=$(( (t_restore - t0) / 1000000 ))
75: edad_s=$(( $(date +%s) - $(date -d "$fecha_respaldo" +%s) ))
76: 
77: echo
78: echo "== Resultado"
79: echo "RTO observado (createdb + pg_restore + validaciones): $((rto_ms / 1000)),$(printf '%03d' $((rto_ms % 1000))) s"
80: echo "   de los cuales createdb + pg_restore:               $((restore_ms / 1000)),$(printf '%03d' $((restore_ms % 1000))) s"
81: echo "RPO observado (antigüedad del respaldo al restaurar):  $((edad_s / 3600)) h $(( (edad_s % 3600) / 60 )) min $((edad_s % 60)) s"
82: if [ "$ok_filas" = 1 ] && [ "$invalidos" = "0 0" ]; then
83:     echo "Validaciones: OK"
84: else
85:     echo "Validaciones: FALLARON"
86: fi
87: echo "La base $ORIGEN no se modificó durante el simulacro."
88: } 2>&1 | tee "$reporte"
89: 
90: grep -q "Validaciones: OK" "$reporte"

1: -- U7 · 01 — Estado del pedido
2: -- El esquema de Food Store no registraba el estado de un pedido, y la consigna de la U7
3: -- trabaja con él (consultas por estado). Se agrega al modelo relacional, que sigue siendo
4: -- la fuente de verdad. Los pedidos nuevos nacen PENDIENTE.
5: -- Los pedidos existentes son datos de prueba: el estado se asigna con una regla fija por id,
6: -- así el resultado es el mismo en cualquier máquina.
7: 
8: DO $$
9: BEGIN
10:     IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_type WHERE typname = 'estado_pedido_enum') THEN
11:         CREATE TYPE estado_pedido_enum AS ENUM ('PENDIENTE', 'CONFIRMADO', 'ENTREGADO', 'CANCELADO');
12:     END IF;
13: END $$;
14: 
15: ALTER TABLE pedido ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS estado estado_pedido_enum NOT NULL DEFAULT 'PENDIENTE';
16: 
17: UPDATE pedido
18:    SET estado = CASE id_pedido % 10
19:                     WHEN 3 THEN 'CANCELADO'
20:                     WHEN 4 THEN 'CONFIRMADO'
21:                     WHEN 5 THEN 'PENDIENTE'
22:                     ELSE 'ENTREGADO'
23:                 END::estado_pedido_enum;
24: 
25: SELECT estado, COUNT(*) AS pedidos FROM pedido GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;

1: #!/usr/bin/env bash
2: # U7 · Consigna 5 — Compara cantidad e IDs de las consultas b) y c) en PostgreSQL y MongoDB

5: cd "$(dirname "$0")"
6: DB="${DB:-foodstore}"

8: mkdir -p evidencias
9: 
10: mongo_ids() {  # $1 = filtro de find()

13: }
14: pg_ids() {  # $1 = condición extra sobre p

19: cantidad() { python_cmd -c "import json,sys; print(len(json.loads(sys.argv[1])))" "$1"; }

<content>
1: // U7 · Carga de los pedidos exportados desde PostgreSQL en MongoDB
2: // Uso (desde esta carpeta): mongosh "mongodb://localhost:27017" --file cargar_mongodb.js
3: // Con Atlas: mongosh "mongodb+srv://..." --file cargar_mongodb.js
4: //
5: // Reglas de integridad que se conservan en la migración:
6: //   R1. total = suma de cantidad × precio_unitario de sus líneas, al centavo.
7: //       Se controla antes de insertar: si un documento no cumple, no se carga ninguno.
8: //   R2. Cada línea tiene cantidad entera > 0 y precio_unitario >= 0, y todo pedido tiene
9: //       al menos una línea. Lo hace cumplir el validador $jsonSchema de la colección,
10: //       también para lo que se inserte después.
11: 
12: const fs = require('fs');
13: 
14: db = db.getSiblingDB('foodstore');
15: 
16: const ESTADOS = ['PENDIENTE', 'CONFIRMADO', 'ENTREGADO', 'CANCELADO'];
17: const FORMAS_PAGO = ['EFECTIVO', 'TARJETA', 'TRANSFERENCIA'];
18: 
19: // '2200.00' -> 220000 centavos, sin pasar por punto flotante
20: function centavos(texto) {
21:   const [entero, dec = ''] = texto.split('.');
22:   return parseInt(entero, 10) * 100 + parseInt((dec + '00').slice(0, 2), 10);
23: }
24: const dinero = (texto) => Decimal128.fromString(texto);
25: 
26: const origen = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('pedidos_export.json', 'utf8'));
27: print(`Documentos leídos de pedidos_export.json: ${origen.length}`);
28: 
29: // R1: control del total antes de convertir nada
30: const errores = origen.filter((p) =>
31:   p.lineas.reduce((s, l) => s + l.cantidad * centavos(l.precio_unitario), 0) !== centavos(p.total));
32: if (errores.length > 0) {
33:   throw new Error(`R1 no se cumple en los pedidos ${errores.map((p) => p._id).join(', ')}: no se carga nada`);
34: }
35: 
36: const documentos = origen.map((p) => ({
37:   _id: p._id,                                   // id_pedido de PostgreSQL
38:   fecha: new Date(p.fecha),
39:   estado: p.estado,
40:   forma_pago: p.forma_pago,
41:   cliente: p.cliente,                           // objeto embebido: id_cliente, nombre, apellido
42:   lineas: p.lineas.map((l) => ({                // arreglo embebido: las líneas del pedido
43:     id_detalle: l.id_detalle,
44:     id_producto: l.id_producto,
45:     producto: l.producto,
46:     categoria: l.categoria,
47:     cantidad: l.cantidad,
48:     precio_unitario: dinero(l.precio_unitario), // precio histórico de la venta
49:     subtotal: dinero(l.subtotal),
50:   })),
51:   total: dinero(p.total),
52:   origen: { motor: 'postgresql', tablas: ['pedido', 'detalle_pedido', 'cliente', 'producto', 'categoria'] },
53: }));
54: 
55: db.pedidos.drop();
56: db.createCollection('pedidos', {
57:   validator: {
58:     $jsonSchema: {
59:       bsonType: 'object',
60:       required: ['_id', 'fecha', 'estado', 'forma_pago', 'cliente', 'lineas', 'total'],
61:       properties: {
62:         _id: { bsonType: ['int', 'long'] },
63:         fecha: { bsonType: 'date' },
64:         estado: { enum: ESTADOS },
65:         forma_pago: { enum: FORMAS_PAGO },
66:         cliente: { bsonType: 'object', required: ['id_cliente', 'nombre', 'apellido'] },
67:         lineas: {
68:           bsonType: 'array',
69:           minItems: 1,
70:           items: {
71:             bsonType: 'object',
72:             required: ['id_producto', 'cantidad', 'precio_unitario'],
73:             properties: {
74:               cantidad: { bsonType: ['int', 'long'], minimum: 1 },
75:               precio_unitario: { bsonType: 'decimal', minimum: 0 },
76:             },
77:           },
78:         },
79:         total: { bsonType: 'decimal', minimum: 0 },
80:       },
81:     },
82:   },
83:   validationAction: 'error',
84: });
85: 
86: const r = db.pedidos.insertMany(documentos, { ordered: true });
87: print(`Documentos insertados: ${Object.keys(r.insertedIds).length}`);
88: 
89: db.pedidos.createIndex({ estado: 1 });
90: db.pedidos.createIndex({ 'lineas.id_producto': 1 });
91: db.pedidos.createIndex({ total: -1 });
92: 
93: print('Validador: un documento con cantidad 0 tiene que ser rechazado');
94: try {
95:   db.pedidos.insertOne({ ...documentos[0], _id: -1, lineas: [{ ...documentos[0].lineas[0], cantidad: 0 }] });
96:   print('  ERROR: se aceptó un documento inválido');
97: } catch (e) {
98:   print(`  Rechazado como se esperaba: ${e.codeName || e.message}`);
99: }
100: db.pedidos.deleteOne({ _id: -1 });   // por si el validador no estuviera activo
101: 
102: print(`Total en la colección: ${db.pedidos.countDocuments()}`);
103: printjson(db.pedidos.findOne({}, { lineas: { $slice: 2 } }));

1: -- U5 · Verificación de permisos: cada rol tiene exactamente lo previsto, ni más ni menos.

3: 
4: \echo '== \du: atributos de los roles'
5: \du rol_*|app_web|admin_datos|usr_*
6: 
7: \echo '== \drg: membresías (PostgreSQL 16+)'
8: \drg rol_*|app_web|admin_datos|usr_*
9: 
10: \echo '== information_schema.role_table_grants (sin admin_datos, que se verifica aparte)'
11: SELECT grantee, table_name, privilege_type
12:   FROM information_schema.role_table_grants
13:  WHERE grantee IN ('rol_app_lectura', 'rol_app_escritura', 'rol_soporte', 'rol_reportes', 'rol_auditor',
14:                    'app_web', 'usr_soporte', 'usr_reportes', 'usr_auditor')
15:  ORDER BY 1, 2, 3;
16: \echo '   Ojo: information_schema no lista las vistas materializadas; por eso la comparación de abajo usa pg_catalog.'
17: 
18: \echo '== Comparación contra la especificación (pg_catalog: tablas, vistas, vistas materializadas, columnas y funciones)'
19: CREATE TEMP TABLE esperado (grantee TEXT, objeto TEXT, privilegio TEXT);
20: INSERT INTO esperado VALUES
21:   ('rol_app_lectura',   'categoria',                     'SELECT'),
22:   ('rol_app_lectura',   'producto',                      'SELECT'),
23:   ('rol_app_lectura',   'pedido',                        'SELECT'),
24:   ('rol_app_lectura',   'detalle_pedido',                'SELECT'),
25:   ('rol_app_lectura',   'vista_productos_vigentes',      'SELECT'),
26:   ('rol_app_escritura', 'pedido',                        'INSERT'),
27:   ('rol_app_escritura', 'detalle_pedido',                'INSERT'),
28:   ('rol_app_escritura', 'producto.stock',                'UPDATE'),
29:   ('rol_app_escritura', 'sp_registrar_pedido()',         'EXECUTE'),
30:   ('rol_app_escritura', 'fn_total_pedido()',             'EXECUTE'),
31:   ('rol_soporte',       'cliente',                       'SELECT'),
32:   ('rol_soporte',       'usuario.id',                    'SELECT'),
33:   ('rol_soporte',       'usuario.nombre',                'SELECT'),
34:   ('rol_soporte',       'usuario.apellido',              'SELECT'),
35:   ('rol_soporte',       'usuario.mail',                  'SELECT'),
36:   ('rol_soporte',       'usuario.celular',               'SELECT'),
37:   ('rol_soporte',       'usuario.rol',                   'SELECT'),
38:   ('rol_soporte',       'usuario.eliminado',             'SELECT'),
39:   ('rol_soporte',       'usuario.created_at',            'SELECT'),
40:   ('rol_soporte',       'usuario.celular',               'UPDATE'),
41:   ('rol_soporte',       'usuario.eliminado',             'UPDATE'),
42:   ('rol_soporte',       'fn_resetear_password()',        'EXECUTE'),
43:   ('rol_reportes',      'mv_facturacion_cat_mes',        'SELECT'),
44:   ('rol_reportes',      'v_top5_categorias',             'SELECT'),
45:   ('rol_reportes',      'vista_productos_vigentes',      'SELECT'),

50: -- usuario_anon se agrega en la Parte D; si ya existe, también se espera para rol_reportes.
51: INSERT INTO esperado SELECT 'rol_reportes', 'usuario_anon', 'SELECT' WHERE to_regclass('public.usuario_anon') IS NOT NULL;
52: 
53: CREATE TEMP VIEW real AS
54: WITH roles AS (
55:     SELECT oid, rolname FROM pg_roles
56:      WHERE rolname IN ('rol_app_lectura', 'rol_app_escritura', 'rol_soporte', 'rol_reportes', 'rol_auditor',
57:                        'app_web', 'usr_soporte', 'usr_reportes', 'usr_auditor')
58: ), tablas AS (
59:     SELECT c.relname AS objeto, (aclexplode(c.relacl)).*
60:       FROM pg_class c
61:      WHERE c.relnamespace = 'public'::regnamespace AND c.relkind IN ('r', 'v', 'm', 'p') AND c.relacl IS NOT NULL
62: ), columnas AS (
63:     SELECT c.relname || '.' || a.attname AS objeto, (aclexplode(a.attacl)).*
64:       FROM pg_attribute a JOIN pg_class c ON c.oid = a.attrelid
65:      WHERE c.relnamespace = 'public'::regnamespace AND a.attacl IS NOT NULL
66: ), rutinas AS (

68:       FROM pg_proc p
69:      WHERE p.pronamespace = 'public'::regnamespace AND p.proacl IS NOT NULL
70: )
71: SELECT r.rolname AS grantee, x.objeto, x.privilege_type AS privilegio
72:   FROM (SELECT * FROM tablas UNION ALL SELECT * FROM columnas UNION ALL SELECT * FROM rutinas) x
73:   JOIN roles r ON r.oid = x.grantee;

75: \echo '   Privilegios DE MÁS (otorgados y no previstos; se esperan 0 filas):'

77: \echo '   Privilegios DE MENOS (previstos y no otorgados; se esperan 0 filas):'

81: SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT (has_table_privilege('admin_datos', c.oid, 'SELECT')
82:                                AND has_table_privilege('admin_datos', c.oid, 'INSERT')
83:                                AND has_table_privilege('admin_datos', c.oid, 'UPDATE')
84:                                AND has_table_privilege('admin_datos', c.oid, 'DELETE'))) AS relaciones_sin_dml_completo,

86:                            OR has_table_privilege('admin_datos', c.oid, 'REFERENCES')
87:                            OR has_table_privilege('admin_datos', c.oid, 'TRIGGER'))       AS relaciones_con_privilegios_extra,
88:        COUNT(*) AS relaciones

90:  WHERE c.relnamespace = 'public'::regnamespace AND c.relkind IN ('r', 'v', 'm', 'p')

94: SELECT t AS tabla,
95:        has_table_privilege('admin_datos', t, 'SELECT') AS lee,
96:        has_table_privilege('admin_datos', t, 'INSERT') AS inserta,
97:        has_table_privilege('admin_datos', t, 'UPDATE') AS modifica,
98:        has_table_privilege('admin_datos', t, 'DELETE') AS borra
99:   FROM unnest(ARRAY['auditoria_seguridad', 'auditoria_precio']) AS t;
100: 
101: \echo '== Membresías esperadas (se esperan 0 diferencias)'
102: WITH esperado_m (miembro, grupo) AS (VALUES
103:     ('app_web', 'rol_app_lectura'), ('app_web', 'rol_app_escritura'),
104:     ('usr_soporte', 'rol_soporte'), ('usr_reportes', 'rol_reportes'), ('usr_auditor', 'rol_auditor')),
105: real_m AS (
106:     SELECT m.rolname AS miembro, g.rolname AS grupo
107:       FROM pg_auth_members am
108:       JOIN pg_roles m ON m.oid = am.member
109:       JOIN pg_roles g ON g.oid = am.roleid
110:      WHERE m.rolname IN ('app_web', 'admin_datos', 'usr_soporte', 'usr_reportes', 'usr_auditor')
111:         OR g.rolname IN ('admin_datos', 'rol_app_lectura', 'rol_app_escritura', 'rol_soporte', 'rol_reportes', 'rol_auditor'))
112: SELECT 'de más' AS tipo, * FROM (SELECT * FROM real_m EXCEPT SELECT * FROM esperado_m) a
113: UNION ALL
114: SELECT 'de menos', * FROM (SELECT * FROM esperado_m EXCEPT SELECT * FROM real_m) b;

117: \set ON_ERROR_STOP off

120: SELECT MIN(id_cliente) AS cli FROM cliente \gset

139: BEGIN; SET ROLE usr_soporte;

141: ROLLBACK;

## Revisión estática U4–U7 y `ejecutar_segunda_entrega.sh`

No modifiqué ningún archivo. `node --check` pasó en los 4 `.js`, `ast.parse` en los 2 `.py`; `psql`/`bash`/`pg_dump` no están en `PATH`, así que las comprobaciones de base quedan como comandos para ejecutar donde esté instalado PostgreSQL.

### Alta

**1. La auditoría de precios deja de registrar quién cambió el precio**
- Archivo: `unidad5_seguridad/sql/01_auth_funciones.sql:96`
- Qué está mal: `ALTER FUNCTION fn_auditar_precios() SECURITY DEFINER ...` hace que la función trigger corra como `postgres`. La columna `auditoria_precio.usuario_bd` tiene `DEFAULT current_user` (`sql/10_auditoria_precios.sql:9`), y dentro de una función `SECURITY DEFINER` `current_user` es el dueño (`postgres`), no `admin_datos`/`app_web`.
- Por qué importa: se rompe la rendición de cuentas: todos los cambios de precio quedan atribuidos a `postgres`.
- Verificación:
```sql
SELECT prosecdef FROM pg_proc WHERE proname = 'fn_auditar_precios';  -- true
BEGIN;
SET ROLE admin_datos;
UPDATE producto SET precio = precio + 1 WHERE id_producto = 1;
RESET ROLE;
SELECT usuario_bd FROM auditoria_precio ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1;  -- se verá postgres, se espera admin_datos
ROLLBACK;
```
Corrección sugerida: `DEFAULT session_user` o insertar `session_user` explícitamente (nota: `fn_resumen_*` en líneas 97-98 también son `SECURITY DEFINER`, pero ahí no hay columna de identidad, así que no tienen este problema).

- Archivo: `unidad5_seguridad/scripts/correr_auditoria_test.sh:34`
- Qué está mal: escribe `extraer_log.py` directamente en `docs/log_auditoria_prueba.txt`, sin pasarlo por `anonimizar_log.py`. El simulacro sí lo hace (`simulacro_incidente.sh:44`).
- Por qué importa: quedan mails e IPs reales en un archivo versionado, al contrario de la política que describe `docs/verificacion_equivalencia.md` y de lo que aplica la Parte D.
- Verificación:
```powershell
Select-String -Path trabajos-practicos\unidad5_seguridad\docs\log_auditoria_prueba.txt -Pattern '[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@'
Select-String -Path trabajos-practicos\unidad5_seguridad\docs\log_auditoria_prueba.txt -Pattern '\d+\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+\('
```

### Media

**3. `configurar_auditoria.sql` no enciende `logging_collector`**
- Archivo: `unidad5_seguridad/sql/configurar_auditoria.sql:12-31`
- Qué está mal: setea `log_connections`, `log_statement`, etc., pero no `logging_collector`; en Windows el valor por defecto es `off`. `pg_current_logfile()` devuelve NULL y `extraer_log.py` falla (`extraer_log.py:20-26`).
- Por qué importa: las evidencias de la Parte B/C de U5 dependen del archivo de log; en una instalación limpia no se generan.
- Verificación:
```sql
SHOW logging_collector;      -- off
SELECT pg_current_logfile(); -- NULL
```
Requiere `ALTER SYSTEM SET logging_collector = 'on'` y reinicio (contexto `postmaster`), no alcanza con `pg_reload_conf()`.

- Qué está mal: `psql -f sql/configurar_auditoria.sql` se ejecuta sin `ON_ERROR_STOP` ni `|| exit`; psql devuelve 0 aunque fallen sentencias. En Mongo, `cargar_mongodb.js` con `|| echo "..."` y los pasos siguientes con `|| true` dejan seguir el flujo con datos viejos o sin colección.

- Verificación:

```
Además, detener MongoDB y correr el orquestador: sigue y termina en 0.

- Archivo: `unidad7_nosql/verificar_consultas.sh:17`

**7. `01_estado_pedido.sql` pisa estados reales en cada ejecución**
- Archivo: `unidad7_nosql/01_estado_pedido.sql:17-23`

\i trabajos-practicos/unidad7_nosql/01_estado_pedido.sql

```

- Archivos: `unidad6_mantenimiento/backup_foodstore.sh:33`, `restore_test.sh:40` y `:45-50`

**10. `verificacion_permisos.sql` no detecta privilegios otorgados a `PUBLIC`**
- Archivo: `unidad5_seguridad/sql/verificacion_permisos.sql:53-73`

-- "DE MÁS" sigue en 0 filas
REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION fn_total_pedido(BIGINT) FROM PUBLIC;
```
